analysis: The item-bias candidate crashed during post-training correctness validation: the host requires positive scores to equal the embedding dot product, but forward adds a learned item bias. Zero initialization does not preserve this equality after training. The highest logged validation HR@10 was 0.645 at epoch 5, below the parent’s 0.650; no strict improvement was observed. Reject this candidate and retain the parent. Future scoring changes must preserve the host’s dot-product identity.
code_summary: NextItNet with length 128, hidden size 64, learned item/position embeddings, and eight independently parameterized residual blocks using dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8]. Each block has two causal width-3 convolutions, LayerNorm, GELU, dropout 0.2, and a learned per-channel residual scale initialized to 0.1. Padding masks and last-nonpadding selection are preserved. The attempted change adds a zero-initialized item-bias embedding to training and candidate scores. LR=0.001, weight decay=0, batch size=128.
